ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all founders, shareholders, directors, authorized signatories and UBOs against the SECO Consolidated Swiss Sanctions List, the UN Security Council Consolidated List, the Swiss Federal Council financial sanctions notices, OFAC SDN and EU sanctions references, and reputable international PEP databases. Any PEP status requires senior-management approval before engagement, enhanced due diligence on source of funds and wealth, and continued monitoring. Standard CDD under AMLA includes identification, UBO verification under the 25% threshold, business-relationship purpose review, and suspicious-transaction reporting to the Money Laundering Reporting Office of Switzerland (MROS). The assessed banking/AML risk tier for this ISIC 4791 online retail merchant is Low_Risk_Standard, subject to Stripe and PayPal card-not-present merchant KYC and ongoing transaction monitoring.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Zentraler Firmenindex ZEFIX (https://www.zefix.ch) operated by the Federal Commercial Register Office and the competent Cantonal Commercial Register Office (Handelsregisteramt)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The company name must be written in Latin script and may use a Swiss national language or an internationally recognized foreign-language designation. Non-Latin names require an official transliteration into Latin characters. The name must not be misleading and must clearly contain the legal-form designation Aktiengesellschaft, AG or SA. The commercial register exercises discretionary review under Swiss Code of Obligations Articles 944 and 956, including distinctiveness, truthfulness, and absence of deception.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: The applicant may request a preliminary name clearance through the relevant Cantonal Commercial Register Office or via a notary public in the canton of the registered office. A formal reservation is granted for an initial 30-day window; an extension may be applied for before expiry by resubmitting the same name and paying a new administrative fee, subject to continued availability. If the name is rejected, the registrar must provide written reasons citing the statutory ground for refusal. The applicant may file an administrative appeal with the cantonal supervisory authority or competent cantonal court within the statutory deadline (generally 10 to 30 days depending on the canton). The appeal should annex the written refusal, a revised alternative name proposal, and evidence of distinctiveness and absence of deceptiveness. After exhaustion of the cantonal remedy, an appeal may be brought to the Swiss Federal Supreme Court.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A pure virtual office or postal mailbox without a physical Swiss address and local administration is not permissible as the registered office of an Aktiengesellschaft. The registered office must be stated in the articles of association and be located in Switzerland. A licensed Swiss fiduciary or corporate-services provider may supply a domiciliation address and substantive administrative support, but this arrangement requires actual management, accounting and board substance in Switzerland. For a garden-hydroponics and home-gardening e-commerce company operating through Stripe and PayPal, an owner-managed office or professional domiciliary arrangement with genuine administration in Switzerland will satisfy the registered-office requirement.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low risk, estimated at approximately 5% for an owner-managed standard e-commerce AG with genuine Swiss management, and approximately 15% for a domicile-only AG using a fiduciary mailbox arrangement. Unannounced physical inspections may occur on reasonable suspicion by tax authorities, anti-money-laundering supervisors, social-insurance regulators or cantonal commercial-register inspection bodies, particularly where UBO filings are inconsistent or corporate substance appears artificial.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Swiss Code of Obligations (Obligationenrecht, OR) Art. 621 et seq. (incorporation), Art. 626 et seq. (contents of articles of association), Art. 629 (election of board), Art. 640 (paid-up capital); Commercial Register Ordinance (Handelsregisterverordnung, HRegV) Art. 38 et seq.; Federal Act on Occupational Pensions (minimum mandatory employee benefits, applied upon first hire).
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Cantonal Commercial Register Office (kantonales Handelsregisteramt) in the registered office canton, e.g., Handelsregisteramt Zürich; central publication through Zefix (Central Business Name Index) and the Swiss Official Gazette of Commerce (SOGC/SHAB).
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Deed of Incorporation certified by a Swiss notary public (öffentliche Beurkundung), accompanied by the Articles of Association (Statuten) and the application for registration in the Commercial Register (Anmeldung zur Handelsregistereintragung).
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: Minimum share capital for an Aktiengesellschaft is CHF 100,000; at least 20% of each nominal share (minimum aggregate CHF 50,000) must be paid up before registration. Paid-up funds must be deposited into a Swiss bank or PostFinance account with a blocking note in favour of the company until registration, and the bank must issue a capital payment confirmation (Liberierungsbestätigung). The funds become freely disposable only after the Commercial Register entry.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: Resolved by the Board of Directors on this day: (1) The issued share capital of CHF 100,000 is accepted, and the founders' subscriptions identified in the deed of incorporation are ratified; the required CHF 50,000 paid-up contribution has been credited to a blocked Swiss bank account and the bank confirmation is approved. (2) The registered office is adopted at the address stated in the Articles of Association, and management authority is granted to the listed corporate officers for all ordinary administrative acts. (3) The Managing Director and the Chairperson of the Board are appointed as authorised officers with sole or collective signature. All filings are delegated to the notary.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Reserve the corporate name and verify the legal form with the Federal Commercial Registry
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Cantonal Commercial Register Office via Zefix and the online name-check portal (easyzefix / Zefix web services)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit a name request to the responsible Cantonal Commercial Register Office or use the Zefix preliminary check. Ensure the company name contains a Swiss-valid legal form suffix (AG/Sàrl/SA) and is not misleading, contrary to public order, or already protected. The chosen name can be technically reserved by a notary through the digital filing platform for a limited period.
required_dossiers: Proposed company name and address of registered office
Legal entity form confirmation (AG)
Articles of Association draft for name compatibility
Certificate or confirmation of no conflicting trade name (search result)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the requested name is refused due to collision or misleading character, file an amendment to the draft articles and resubmit via the notary through the Commercial Register Office within 10 days; no formal appeal fee applies at this stage.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Notarise the incorporation deed and the Articles of Association
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Cantonal Civil Law Notary (öffentliche Notarin / Notar) in the registered office canton
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Convene the founders and execute the deed of incorporation and the complete Articles of Association before a Swiss notary. The notary verifies legal capacity, capital contributions, names, share counts, and quorum. The deed must state the share capital, share categories, and special auditing decisions. After notarisation, the notary issues a notarial deed and submits the registration application electronically to the Commercial Register Office.
required_dossiers: Valid identity documents or extracts of the commercial register for all founders
Draft Articles of Association (Statuten)
List of subscribers and nominal shares
Statement on in-kind contributions, if any
Bank capital payment confirmation (Liberierungsbestätigung)
Notarisation instruction form
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notary identifies formal defects, execute an amendment deed or supplementary contract and re-notarise; the notary issues a revised deed and resubmits within the pending registration period.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: File the registration application with the Cantonal Commercial Register
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Cantonal Commercial Register Office (Handelsregisteramt) through the notary's electronic submission portal
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The notary files the incorporation application electronically, attaching the notarial deed, articles of association, corporate officer declarations with specimen signatures, and confirmation of capital payment. The Commercial Register conducts formal legal review against mandatory provisions of the Swiss Code of Obligations, registers the company, and assigns the Commercial Register number and Legal Entity Identifier (LEI).
required_dossiers: Notarised deed of incorporation
Certified copy of the Articles of Association
List of board members with specimen signatures (unterschriftsbeglaubigte Erklärung)
Bank capital payment confirmation
Declaration by board members regarding registration
Power of attorney for the notary, if applicable
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Commercial Register issues a request for supplement, provide clarifications or rectified declarations through the notary within the set deadline (commonly 10 business days) and pay any supplementary administrative fee; otherwise the application is returned and a fresh filing is required.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Register with the Federal Tax Administration for VAT and social security purposes
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Federal Tax Administration (Eidgenössische Steuerverwaltung, ESTV) and your cantonal social insurance institution (e.g., Suisse/Sammelstiftung for AHV/IV/EO), plus cantonal tax office
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After Commercial Register registration, the company is automatically registered or must actively file for VAT (Mehrwertsteuer) using the formular 101 if annual worldwide turnover exceeds CHF 100,000. Register as employer with the cantonal compensation office to obtain an AHV employer number, and confirm the obligation to withhold income tax from employees. The canton will issue a cantonal tax file number and industrial/commercial registry extracts (WEF extract).
required_dossiers: Commercial register extract (Handelsregisterauszug)
Formular 101 for VAT registration
Employer registration form for AHV/IV/EO/ALV
Proof of registered office address
Passport or ID of authorised representative
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If VAT registration is queried due to missing business description, amend the company purpose in the articles or provide supplementary information to ESTV; any late registration penalty can be waived if the delay is administratively negligible and initial turnover below threshold.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Open the corporate bank account and obtain the paid-up capital confirmation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Licensed Swiss bank or PostFinance (client services for legal entities)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Book the signed-up share capital payments to an escrow-like blocked account opened in the company name or a founder-account specifically dedicated to the company. Submit the resolution and draft articles to the bank. The bank performs beneficial-owner due diligence under the Swiss Anti-Money Laundering Act and releases the blocked capital after the Commercial Register registration has been evidenced, simultaneously issuing the Liberierungsbestätigung for submission.
required_dossiers: Articles of association (notarised or draft with approval)
Incorporation deed excerpt
Commercial register extract, once available
Beneficial ownership declaration (Form A)
Identity documents of authorised signatories and beneficial owners
Resolution of the board specifying the account purpose
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If due diligence is incomplete, the bank issues a request for information; the applicant must resubmit a corrected beneficial owner declaration and updated ID documents. If refusal persists, apply simultaneously to two systemically relevant banks or to a private bank specialising in FinTech e-commerce entities.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Publish the incorporation notice and fulfil SHAB publication and corporate governance requirements
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Swiss Official Gazette of Commerce (SHAB) / Federal Commercial Registry and cantonal organisations
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The Commercial Register triggers the mandatory publication of the registration in the SOGC/SHAB, including company name, legal form, registered office, purpose, share capital, and authorised representatives. The board then convenes its first organisational meeting to adopt financial year calendar, determine internal control measures, decide on the authorised signatories, and approve any closure-of-year provisions.
required_dossiers: Commercial register extract with publication date
Notice of general meeting and board meeting minutes
Declaration of acceptance of functions by each board member
Bank account proof and share capital confirmation
Status of infrastructure and office lease agreement
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If SHAB publication contains errors, file a rectification request with the Commercial Register Office; the correction is published at no charge if the registry caused the error. If board members fail to attend the organisational meeting, use written circular resolution, but all mandatory statutory governance documents must be signed by each director.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Not required for pure e-commerce distribution; if warehousing or packing is carried out, the relevant authority is the Cantonal Trade Office (Kantonales Gewerbeamt) and the Federal Office for Customs and Border Security (FOCBS) for import of equipment. No factory or industrial manufacturing permit is necessary.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: No statutory operating license (Bewilligung) is required for online retail of hydroponic gardening equipment under Swiss law, provided the business is carried out as a registered commercial enterprise and complies with product safety and consumer information rules.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Federal Office for the Environment (FOEN / BAFU) and Cantonal Environmental Protection Agency (kantonales Amt für Umweltschutz)
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt from formal Environmental Impact Assessment (UVP/EIA) under the Swiss Environmental Impact Assessment Ordinance for online retail warehousing and office use; no category is triggered because no significant release of pollutants or large-scale physical plant is involved.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Only household-scale wastewater and office waste from leased premises apply; must meet local municipal sewer discharge standards. Packaging waste and transport packaging placed on the Swiss market must comply with the Swiss Packaging Regulation and the principles of the Federal Act on Environmental Protection (Umweltschutzgesetz), including take-back and recycling schemes. No VOCs, industrial wastewater, or hazardous substances are generated.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety clearance for the rented office/warehouse is confirmed by the local fire inspection authority (Gebäudeversicherung / Feuerpolizei) through a land-use and occupancy confirmation. Structural load inspections are not required for non-industrial commercial units. Workplace hygiene and occupational safety for handling of packaging and computer environments follow the Swiss Labour Act (Arbeitsgesetz) and SUVA directives for office workplaces; electrical equipment must bear CE markings and satisfy the Swiss Technical Inspection Association (Swiss TS) conformity requirements.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Swiss Federal Tax Administration (Eidgenössische Steuerverwaltung ESTV / Administration fédérale des contributions AFC / Amministrazione federale delle contribuzioni AFC), www.estv.admin.ch; VAT portal 'eService ESTV' and UID register at www.uid.admin.ch; customs export clearance via Federal Office for Customs and Border Security (FOCBS), www.bazg.admin.ch ('e-dec' export declaration system).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: For a Swiss AG (CH_AG): (1) Incorporate via notarial deed and commercial register entry (Handelsregisteramt) which auto-allocates the UID (CHE-123.456.789); (2) register for VAT with ESTV within 30 days of commencing taxable activity (Art. 67 MWSTG), using form 901/902 or eService, obtaining VAT ID 'CHE-xxx.xxx.xxx MWST'; (3) register with cantonal tax administration at registered office for profit/capital tax; (4) register as employer with AHV compensation office for social security; (5) if acting as importer of record, obtain a customs client account at FOCBS or use a licensed customs agent. For a foreign entity without Swiss residence: mandatory VAT registration with ESTV as soon as Swiss taxable turnover reaches CHF 100,000 (Art. 10 para 2 MWSTG); voluntary registration is available to claim input VAT refunds (Art. 12 MWSTG).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation (Swiss AG is a per-se corporation taxable on net profit at federal 8.5% plus cantonal/communal rates, 11.9%–21% combined effective; unlimited worldwide taxation with territorial carve-outs: foreign permanent establishments and foreign immovable property are exempt in most cantons, and the participation deduction exempts qualifying dividend/capital-gain income; no pass-through, no transparency).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No US-style check-the-box regime and no hybrid-mismatch elections in Swiss law; anti-hybrid rules implementing BEPS Action 2 apply compulsorily to AGs from 1 January 2020 (Art. 58a DBG, Art. 9a StHG). Available elections/options: (a) VAT group election under Art. 21 MWSTG; (b) voluntary VAT registration by foreign suppliers without Swiss PE (Art. 12 MWSTG); (c) option to tax export-related services? (No — rather:) (c) application for advance tax ruling with ESTV/canton on participation relief, transfer pricing or patent-box treatment; (d) cantonal patent box (Patentbox) and R&D super-deduction elections requiring a ruling; (e) partial input VAT recovery methods (Art. 42–43 MWSTG) election (switching between calculation methods may be subject to ESTV approval).

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Swiss National Bank (SNB) — Schweizerische Nationalbank / Banque nationale suisse, exercising monetary and statistical oversight; the Federal Department of Finance (FDF) and State Secretariat for International Financial Matters (SIF) supervise financial market policy but Switzerland maintains no discretionary foreign-exchange control authority.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Switzerland applies full current and capital account convertibility under the Swiss Federal Constitution and the Federal Act on Currency and Payment Instruments. Profits, dividends, royalties, and capital proceeds are freely transferable without exchange-control approval. The Swiss franc is a freely floating, fully convertible hard currency with no investor registration, repatriation licensing, or residual non-resident restrictions. Commercial banks execute cross-border payments subject to Swiss anti-money-laundering and economic-sanctions screening only; there are no convertibility barriers or profit-remittance taxes beyond ordinary withholding taxes where applicable.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: There is no statutory surrender requirement, obligatory conversion ratio, or mandated repatriation timeline for export receipts in Switzerland. Swiss exporters retain full discretion over currency denomination, timing, and holding of foreign currency. SNB reporting obligations apply only to banks for statistical balance-of-payments purposes on cross-border payment transactions (threshold-based, not approval-based); enterprises are not required to convert export proceeds into CHF or to hold them within Switzerland.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility rating: Low-to-Medium. Swiss law does not recognize passported EU e-money institutions (EMIs) as banks; a non-bank EMI may execute payments solely as a payment service provider under the Swiss Payment Services Act (PSA), but such providers require FINMA licensing or a licensing-exemption structure and cannot hold client deposits in the same manner as a bank. Offshore digital EMIs without a Swiss license may operate only via commercial agency arrangements with a Swiss licensed financial intermediary for Swiss-sourced payments; however, their viability for long-term treasury clearing and capital escrow is low due to heightened AML scrutiny on virtual-currency farms and non-bank fintech platforms. A Swiss AG is therefore advised to use a regulated Tier-1 bank as the primary liquidity account and to use EMIs solely as downstream collection channels for low-value online card payments.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: For newly formed Swiss AGs with non-resident shareholders or directors, most Swiss Tier-1 banks require physical presence of at least one authorized signatory (typically the chairman or managing director) for the introductory and compliance interview. Remote opening is possible for simplified Swiss-resident companies without a beneficial-ownership complexity, using video identification and Swiss e-ID/electronic passport verification, but for cross-border e-commerce structures involving foreign directors or a corporate ownership chain, banks generally mandate an in-person interview at a Swiss branch or via a Swiss-registered fiduciary agent with a power of attorney. The board may delegate KYC attendance to a Swiss resident signatory provided full notarized powers are executed and the UBO declaration is personally certified.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Beneficial ownership chain comprising opaque offshore entities or nominee shareholders
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Organizational chart identifying all natural-person UBOs; certified corporate registers of each intermediate entity; notarized declarations of trust; audited or management financial statements; explanation of commercial rationale for any offshore intermediate; source-of-wealth documentation for initial capital deposits.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Merchant business classified under 'garden goods' with ambiguous digital sales model, raising potential cross-border B2C fraud or sanctions concerns
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Valid ISIC/NACE classification certificate; website terms of sale and delivery; customer due-diligence procedures for high-volume retail receipts; PCI-DSS compliance certificate for Stripe/PayPal integration; historical transaction records proving low chargeback rates; documented supplier and logistics contracts.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Unusual capital injection pattern: quick succession of IPO or crowdfunding wire transfers from unrelated foreign payers, typical of money mules or investment fraud
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Notarized subscription agreements or convertible-loan deeds; bank statements of initiating accounts; legal source-of-funds declarations for each wire; capital contribution registers (Aktienbuch); tax identification numbers of shareholders; proof that payments correspond to statutory share capital or authorized reserves.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Cross-border outbound payments to jurisdictions with sanctioned or high-risk counterparties (e.g., equipment components from neighboring non-EEA states)
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Full trade-contract trail; HS Harmonised System codes for hydroponics equipment; export/import customs declarations (Swiss e-dec); packaging and labeling compliance; embargo checks on all counterparties; insurance and shipping invoices; statement from a Swiss external counsel confirming no sanctions nexus.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Cryptocurrency or digital-asset adjacency: entities with crypto-linked clientele or payment acceptance beyond traditional card rails
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Legitimate product catalogue for hydroponic non-cannabis horticulture; certification that goods are legal plant-growing equipment; detailed payment-rail description; negative anti-drug-trafficking compliance statement; monitoring and transaction filtering system for explicit crypto or cannabis exposures; board resolution disclaiming illicit cultivation use.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Inbound capital injections to the Swiss AG’s operational or capital escrow account must comply with the Swiss Code of Obligations (share capital deposit requirements) and bank-internal AML circulars. Wires should be executed via SWIFT MT103 or SEPA CT with full Originator and Beneficiary information. Swiss banks do not require a proprietary 'purpose code', but for statistical and clearing purposes you must include the commercial reference (e.g., 'Share Capital Subscription', 'Convertible Loan', 'Trade Receivable Payment') and remit using the Beneficiary's IBAN (CH + national clearings via SIC). Verification at the receiving bank will demand the underlying capital subscription documentation and a completed Form A (disclosure of beneficial owner) if not already held. The recommended compliant routing is: overseas payer bank – correspondent Swiss bank (typically UBS/ZKB) – SIC/PostFinance clearing – Swiss AG’s IBAN. All funds must settle in CHF or the nominated foreign-currency account and be booked under the correct economic purpose account to avoid automatic blockage by money-laundering filters.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: For trade disbursements, the Swiss AG uses standard clearing methods: (i) SWIFT MT103 for direct correspondent-bank transfers, with mandatory structured remittance information (e.g., invoice number, ISIC order reference); (ii) SWIFT MT202/MT202 COV for bank-to-bank interbank settlements underlying an MT103; (iii) commercial letters of credit opened via MT700 with the confirming bank, ensuring documentary compliance under UCP600; (iv) SEPA credit transfers for EEA-based creditors, with full EUR transfer via STEP2/EACHA inter-bank infrastructure. For online retail payments incoming from Stripe/PayPal, treasury settlements are made by these PSPs to the Swiss bank account via domestic ACH or international SWIFT; outbound supplier payments above EUR 10,000 should be sent by MT103 rather than card to preserve audit trails and avoid merchant-of-record liability. Swiss banks perform real-time screening of counterparties and sanction lists on all outbound payment messages; no exchange-control license is required, but the mandate to supply the payment reference is mandatory for reconciliation and anti-money-laundering review.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Plain vanilla deliverable FX forwards (CHF/EUR/CHF/USD) executed bilaterally with Swiss or OECD-domiciled credit institutions under a market-standard ISDA master agreement
Currency swaps (fixed-to-fixed and floating-to-fixed) for medium-term hedging of foreign-currency commercial borrowings or trade receivables, subject to FINMA conduct rules on non-bank counterparties

Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) in illiquid exotic currencies (e.g., offshore CNY) where legal delivery is impossible; CHF must be the settlement currency and the transaction must reference a genuine underlying cross-border trade exposure
FX options (EUR/USD against CHF) under the FINMA-recognized simplified options rules for corporate hedgers, provided the option is not speculative and is booked for transaction hedging
Cross-currency interest rate swaps (CIRS) for matching assets and liabilities in different currencies where the Swiss company holds material foreign trade receivables or financings

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual shareholders' meeting minutes approving the annual financial statements and profit appropriation
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Shareholders' General Meeting (internal corporate organ; minutes retained at registered office)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within six months after the balance-sheet date (Art. 698 para. 4 CO)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: No administrative strike-off; delaying resolution invalidates dividend distributions and exposes the board to personal civil and criminal liability

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual financial statements and statutory audit report filed with the Commercial Register
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Commercial Register Office of the Canton of Zug (Handelsregisteramt)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within twelve months after the balance-sheet date, applicable only to companies subject to an ordinary audit (Art. 906 CO)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Formal reminder from the register office, administrative fine up to CHF 5,000, and in persistent default compulsory dissolution or administrative strike-off after prior warning

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual corporate income tax return for federal and cantonal income tax and capital tax
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Tax Administration of the Canton of Zug (Steuerverwaltung Zug)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Due by 31 March of the year following the tax period; extension generally granted to 30 September upon request
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Default interest, disciplinary fine up to CHF 8,000, forfeiture of extension privileges, authority's default assessment, and criminal tax proceedings for intentional understatement

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Swiss VAT return (quarterly settlement; semi-annual or annual settlement available on approval)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Federal Tax Administration (Eidgenössische Steuerverwaltung ESTV / FTA)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 60 days after the end of each settlement period; electronic filing deadline may be extended
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Reminder procedure, default assessment, procedural administrative fine, default interest at 5% per annum, and criminal penalties for deliberate tax evasion

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual AHV/AVS wage statement and social security declaration for employees
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Compensation office for old-age and survivors' insurance (AHV-Ausgleichskasse / ZAS)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Due by 31 January of the following calendar year for the completed payroll year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Contribution arrears with interest, administrative penalty for late or incomplete wage statements, and enforcement proceedings against the employer

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Ordinary full audit is compulsory if, for two consecutive financial years, the AG exceeds any two of the three statutory thresholds: balance-sheet total CHF 20,000,000; annual turnover CHF 40,000,000; annual average of 250 full-time employees. Full audit also applies to listed companies, bond issuers, and on demand of shareholders holding 10% of the share capital. A limited review audit applies above the opting-out threshold; an AG with fewer than ten full-time employees on annual average may validly dispense with any audit by unanimous shareholder resolution.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Swiss Code of Obligations accounting law (Art. 957–962 CO); Swiss GAAP FER for statutory SME financial statements; IFRS mandatory for listed groups and permitted for individual statutory accounts

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Switzerland does not currently require an annual beneficial-owner confirmation filing for an ordinary AG. The board must continuously update the Commercial Register, maintain the share register (Aktienbuch) recording every transfer of registered shares, and keep the register of bearer shareholders where bearer shares exist. For banking and AML purposes, the e-commerce entity must identify and document beneficial owners when engaging financial intermediaries. A federal beneficial-owner register is expected to become mandatory for AGs after the entry into force of the 2024 AML transparency revision.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Business books, accounting records and supporting vouchers

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 1,800–6,000 per annum for fiduciary registered-office, domiciliation and corporate-secretarial services in Zug and central Switzerland
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 3,500–12,000 for a limited review audit; USD 15,000–40,000 for a full ordinary audit; nil where the unanimous audit opting-out resolution is validly adopted and recorded

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 8.5% federal corporate income tax assessed on pre-federal-tax net profit (effective federal rate 7.83%); combined federal + cantonal + communal effective rate for an Aktiengesellschaft in the Canton of Zug is approximately 11.9% (2025).
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: No holiday-style tax exemptions. Available shields: (i) cantonal Patent Box exempting up to 90% of qualifying net IP income (federal: 10% exemption); (ii) cantonal R&D super-deduction up to 150% of eligible costs (e.g., Zug: 100% base plus 50% additional); (iii) notional interest deduction for surplus equity in selected cantons; (iv) VAT rules: 8.1% standard, 2.6% accommodation, 0% for exported cross-border e-commerce.
